summary: 16-bit image blit with transparent-color support. Stores the transparent color a7 into the global dword_5DD804, computes per-row source/destination strides from the 16-bit pixel width a5, then dispatches on the guard (a7 != 0xFFFF || (2*a5 & 7) != 0): the per-pixel path copies each word from the source to the destination except pixels equal to the transparent color, while the aligned-0xFFFF fast path copies 64-bit MMX chunks (2*a5 >> 3 QWORDs per row) plus a byte tail, row by row for a6 rows.

operations.description: Store the transparent color argument a7 into the global transparent-color register dword_5DD804.
Compute byte width v10 = 2 * a5 and the per-row source/destination strides v17 = a2 - v10 and v18 = a4 - v10.
Dispatch on (a7 != 0xFFFF || (v10 & 7) != 0): take the per-pixel transparent-copy path, otherwise take the aligned 64-bit fast path.
Per-pixel path: nested do-while loops over a5 columns per row and a6 rows.

Per-pixel copy: read the next 16-bit pixel from the source pointer (this field 0x0, the source pixel data) and write it to the destination only when it differs from dword_5DD804, i.e. transparent pixels are skipped; advance both pointers.
Advance source/destination pointers to the next row by v17/v18 at the end of each row in the per-pixel path.
Fast path: 64-bit MMX copy loop, v10 >> 3 QWORDs per row, over a6 rows.
Fast path tail: qmemcpy the remaining (v10 & 7) bytes per row when the width is not 8-byte aligned, and advance both pointers by that remainder.
Advance source/destination pointers by v17/v18 between rows in the fast path.
Return void; _m_empty() performs MMX-state cleanup before returning.

clean_pseudocode: void ImageBlitTransparent16(_WORD *src, int srcRowStride, _WORD *dst, int dstRowStride, int widthPixels, int heightRows, unsigned short transparent) {
if ((rowBytes & 7) != 0) { memcpy(dst, src, rowBytes & 7); src = (_WORD *)((char *)src + (rowBytes & 7)); dst = (_WORD *)((char *)dst + (rowBytes & 7)); }
unresolved: Semantic role of dword_5DD804 beyond the transparent-color comparison is unknown; the global persists across calls.
The 0xFFFF + 8-byte-aligned case assumes the source has no transparent pixels and performs a raw 64-bit copy; whether callers guarantee that is caller-dependent.
Pixel format (RGB565 or similar) and the meaning of the row strides a2/a4 depend on the caller's image layout.
